Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I put together a concise proposal for your upcoming Dedicated renewal and the capacity/scale policy changes Aurora requested. High-level summary:

- Committed increase: +20 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (bringing total reserved pool to 80 GPUs)
- Autoscale policy adjustments: set min replicas = 6 (previously 4), max replicas = 48, warm pool = 8 GPUs (reserved, pre-initialized), target scale-up lag SLA = 8s (p95) for cold->warm transitions
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 2.0M tokens/min sustained per region (US East) with burst headroom to 2.8M tokens/min for 15 minutes during traffic spikes
- Term: 12 months starting Jan 1 2027; 15% commit discount on GPU hourly rates for the additional capacity line item

Notes on billing and warm pool: warm pool GPUs are billed as reserved capacity (flat hourly) but are configured to be available immediately for low-latency traffic; burst beyond reserved capacity is billed at the burst rate (we included a burst credit buffer in the attached pricing sheet).

Attachments: Aurora_Dedicated_Renewal_SOW.pdf (SOW + service levels), redwood-dedicated-pricing-2026.xlsx (line-item pricing + discount).

Action items / ask from Aurora: please confirm acceptance of the proposed min/max replica counts, warm pool size, and the Jan 1 start date so we can prepare the amendment and route to DocuSign. If you want Karthik or Marcus looped in for any deeper infra/latency questions, happy to include them.

Best,

Alex — quick answers from infra and commercial side: 

1) Warm pool billing: warm pool GPUs are charged at the reserved rate (flat hourly) and are not charged additional per-token when they are actively serving. We do not double-bill.

2) Burst capacity: burst beyond reserved pool is billed at the burst rate automatically. We include a 48-hour notification window for customers currently consuming >50% of burst for >30 minutes so that we can discuss converting that headroom to reserved capacity if needed; however, billing switches to burst rates immediately when used. We can add a mid-term uplift clause at the pre-negotiated pricing — approved on our end.

3) Instrumentation & validation: Redwood Console will expose the token-level latency charts, per-route p95/p99, and a scale-event timeline. We also provide a temporary shared dashboard link during ramp for 30 days. For SLA evidence we can provide traces for specific scale events and a weekly ramp report. Karthik — can you confirm we can provide a 30-day shared dashboard link and the trace exports?

4) Legal/contract: commercial approves the Jan 1, 2027 start date and a one-time mid-term uplift option (subject to PO and 60-day lead time for committed capacity changes). We will prepare an amendment that includes the min/max replica counts, warm pool size, and the target scale-up SLA. Marcus — please attach the updated pricing sheet with the 15% discount for the new reserved GPUs.
